September 1, 2026

Democrats continue to have an edge over Republicans in vote intent for the November elections for U.S. Congress, according to the latest Economist / YouGov Poll. 46% of registered voters say they will vote for the Democratic Party candidate in their district, and 40% will vote for the Republican candidate. That 6-point Democratic lead among registered voters is in line with recent weeks, and larger than the Democrats' low-single-digit lead for much of the summer. According to the latest RealClearPolling' generic Congressional voting polls, 48.7% said they'd vote Democrat, 42% said they'd vote Republican.

In the latest generic congressional voting poll by Economist/YouGov, 39% said if elections for Congress were being held today, they'd vote for the Democratic candidate compared to 32% that said Republican. A whopping 30% said other, not sure or that they would not vote at all.

But a closer look at individual polls suggests the battle for Congress may be far from settled.
